title: Showcase: the upgrade, proven
summary: Present the mBot upgrade and its before-and-after numbers to the family, and take one real question from them about the proof.
materials: mBot v1.2 with the week 11 upgrade fitted
the fixed test course from week 11
tri-fold science fair board or a large sheet of card
the Maker's Log, open to week 11

steps.title: Plan the presentation
steps.body:
Set up the same test course from week 11 exactly as it was. Write the six before-and-after numbers on the science fair board, large enough to read from across the room.

Plan the presentation in this order.

1. Show the mBot as it was before the upgrade and say what problem the upgrade was meant to fix.

2. Show the upgrade itself and which parts of the sprint it came from: a printed part, a circuit, a mechanism.

3. Run the course live with the upgrade fitted, once, in front of the family.

4. Show the board's before-and-after numbers and say whether the difference was bigger than the wobble between runs.

Be ready for one question from the family about the proof itself, such as how many times it was tested or what could have made the numbers unfair.

figure.alt: The mBot with its upgrade runs the same fixed course from start to finish while the family watches. A science fair board nearby displays the six before-and-after numbers from the test.

steps.title: Rehearse the run and the answer
steps.body:
Run the course once at demo speed before the family sees it, on the same course used for the real numbers. Nothing about the setup should have quietly changed since week 11.

Practise the sentence that states the result honestly: whether the after number really beat the before number by more than the wobble, or whether the evidence was closer than that. A true small result said plainly beats a big result that overstates what the data showed.
checklist: The course matches the one used for the week 11 numbers
The board shows all six real before-and-after numbers
The live run completes on the same course as the recorded numbers
I can answer one question about how the test was made fair, honestly

steps.title: Show the family
steps.body:
Gather the family and run the presentation in the order rehearsed: the before robot, the upgrade, the live run, and the board's numbers. Invite one question from the family about the proof and answer it as honestly as the data allows.

End by naming one thing that would make the test fairer next time, since every real experiment has a next version that would tighten it up.

steps.title: Show it
steps.prompt: A short recording of the live run and the family's question being answered, plus a photo of the board with all six numbers
